title: 2026-10-22_Linux_AirDropBot_Botnet_Investigation_155
description: Investigate and respond to the Linux/AirDropBot botnet activity on the network.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: The network has experienced unusual traffic patterns and potential security incidents. Your task is to investigate and respond to these issues.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content:
You have SSH access to the victim host with the following credentials:
- Hostname: victim
- Username: ubuntu
- Password: ubuntu

Enter 'start' to begin the investigation.
levels.local_content:
Local sandbox access is not required for this scenario. Use the following credentials to access the victim host:
- Hostname: victim
- Username: ubuntu
- Password: ubuntu

Enter 'start' to begin the investigation.

levels.title: Identify Suspicious Service
levels.content:
Identify and investigate an unauthorized or suspicious service responsible for periodic external communication.

**Question:** What is the name of the suspicious service that is beaconing to an external server?
levels.solution: Check running services and look for unusual network connections. The suspicious service is likely named `bot-beacon-cloudprocess`. Use the command `systemctl list-units --type=service` to list all services.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Check running services and look for unusual network connections.

levels.title: Identify Abnormal Network Traffic Service
levels.content:
Identify the service responsible for generating abnormal volumes of network traffic.

**Question:** What is the name of the service generating the abnormal network traffic?
levels.solution: Examine systemd timers and services for unusual activity. The service generating abnormal network traffic is likely named `bot-flood-cloudprocess`. Use the command `systemctl list-timers` to list all timers.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Examine systemd timers and services for unusual activity.

levels.title: Determine Persistence Mechanism
levels.content:
Determine how the suspicious service is automatically started after reboot.

**Question:** What is the persistence mechanism used by the suspicious service?
levels.solution: Investigate systemd timers and services for clues about how the service maintains persistence. The persistence mechanism is likely a systemd timer named `system-update-checker.timer`. Use the command `systemctl list-timers --all` to list all timers.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Investigate systemd timers and services for clues about how the service maintains persistence.
